### User stories

| Role | I want to | So that |
|---|---|---|
| Caregiver | Have my son's birth doses from abroad recognised at home | his care does not start over and nothing is repeated |
| Caregiver | Show each family member's records abroad from our one shared phone, with a passcode I can say aloud | a doctor abroad can treat us without paper or an app |
| Caregiver | Decide who sees my child's record, and for how long | the record stays at home and I know who has looked |
| Birth clinic vaccinator | Print a signed record of each birth dose the family can carry anywhere |  |
| Community health worker | Read a foreign vaccination QR offline and register the child with it | the clinic sees what was given before the family arrives |
| Community health worker | Refer a child whose foreign record needs checking | verification is done by someone who can |
| Community health worker | Register a newborn into the household offline, before civil registration | no newborn in my village is missed, even with no signal |
| Home clinic provider | Know whether a foreign certificate is genuine, and why not when it is not |  |
| Home clinic provider | See which doses are due once the foreign doses are imported | I give only what is missing |
| Home clinic provider | Keep the foreign vaccine code and add our schedule code beside it, deciding myself when there is no match | the other country's record is never overwritten and the next nurse need not decide again |
| Point-of-care provider | Read a visiting child's summary and vaccinations from a QR the parent shows | without installing anything or calling another country |
| Point-of-care provider | Know the record I read abroad came from the child's home country and was not altered | I can rely on it as I would on my own clinic's record |
{: .grid }

### User scenarios

Each step names the requirements of
[smart-trust-tools](https://github.com/litlfred/smart-trust-tools/tree/main/skills/requirements)
it exercises, and the FHIR examples of this guide it produces. The stories are
in [`scenarios/stories.json`](https://github.com/litlfred/smart-trust-demo/blob/main/scenarios/stories.json).
Each moment ends with its pain point, what enables it, and the policy point it
makes, as the VaxLink walkthrough presents them.

#### J1 — Born abroad (Thailand, birth day)

**Precondition: the issuer's DSC is on the trust list.** XXR's document
signer certificate (DSC), issued under XXR's Country Signing CA (CSCA), was
shared with the GDHCN, the Trust Anchor, before any DVC is signed; the GDHCN
publishes it as a DID document. Sharing it is not a step of issuing. A DVC
signed with a key whose DSC was never shared fails every receiver's
trust-list check ([STT-VER-006](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-006)).

Khamla gives birth to Somsack on 2025-10-28 at Chiang Rai Provincial
Hospital, away from home. He has no Thai identity number. Dr Somchai gives the
Hep B and BCG birth doses and records them with their WHO PreQual product
codes. For each dose, the hospital system does three things:

1. It builds a DVCMinPreQual payload: [STT-PAY-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-pay-001)…[005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-pay-005) and [STT-PAY-007](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-pay-007), with subclaim −6 ([STT-SEL-003](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-sel-003)). No identity document is needed ([STT-PAY-005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-pay-005)).
2. It prepares the CWT and the bytes to sign: [STT-CWT-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cwt-001)…[005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cwt-005), [STT-ISS-004](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-iss-004).
3. It has XXR's key sign them ([STT-COS-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cos-002), [STT-COS-006](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cos-006)), then finishes the HC1 text: [STT-COS-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cos-001), [STT-ZIP-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-zip-001), [STT-B45-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-b45-001), [STT-HC1-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-hc1-001), [STT-QR-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-qr-001).

Khamla leaves with two paper DVCs.
*In the demo:* the library tests use the WHO guide's own two signed HC1
strings ([QR Code Generation §12](https://smart.who.int/trust/qr_code_generation.html)),
which verify against the live DEV trust list under the same XXR key. Somsack's
DVC payloads are illustrative, as in VaxLink. Live issuance in the app uses a
TEST-ONLY key ([STT-ISS-003](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-iss-003)), whose DSC is not on the GDHCN list, so its DVCs
do not verify in J3.

- *Pain point:* without a national id, the records would stay locked in the Thai hospital's system.
- *Enabler:* a signed QR card travels with the family; no id or database lookup is needed.
- *Policy:* babies born abroad can get a verifiable vaccine record without the host country's civil registration or national id.

#### J2 — Found at home (Lao PDR, 3 weeks later)

**J2a.** On a routine visit to Village 04, Soukanh finds a newborn the Lao
system does not know exists. Her phone has had no signal for weeks. On the
CHW app's newborn form (structured data capture, `TrustDemoHouseholdRegistration`)
she adds Somsack to the Sengmany household (`TrustDemoHousehold`), with a
temporary id. Bounmy confirms the details as head of household.

**J2b.** Khamla shows the two cards. The CHW app reads them with
**read-unverified** ([STT-VER-011](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-011); [STT-B45-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-b45-002), [STT-ZIP-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-zip-002), [STT-CBR-003](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-cbr-003)),
which needs no trust list. It shows the doses and saves them as reported by
the family, not verified (`TrustDemoJ2HepBReported`, `TrustDemoJ2BcgReported`:
`primarySource` false). Soukanh refers Somsack to the district health center
(`TrustDemoJ2Referral`). Everything stays queued on the phone, for 28 days if
need be, and syncs when it next reaches a signal.

- *Pain point:* babies born abroad are invisible to the home system until civil registration catches up; without a check, a forged or mistyped card could become an official record.
- *Enabler:* an offline form links the baby to his household at once, and the app keeps what the family reported apart from what has been verified.
- *Policy:* newborns can be registered at home, offline, before an id exists; and trust is not granted too early.

#### J3 — Made official (Vientiane District Health Center, 4 weeks later)

**Precondition: the DID documents are already loaded.** Loading them is not
a step of this visit. The clinic may be offline all day, so the EHR fetches
nothing during it: its trust store holds the GDHCN DEV trust list as it was
last refreshed, including XXR's DSC DID document ([STT-TRU-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-001), [STT-TRU-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-002),
[STT-TRU-005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-005)). A clinic with no connection of its own refreshes it about weekly,
when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office, where Country
B retrieves the list the GDHCN trust anchor distributes. A DSC published after that refresh is not in
the clinic's copy, so its DVC fails the trust-list check ([STT-VER-006](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-006)) until
the next refresh.

**J3a.** Nurse Chanthasone opens the referral and scans the QRs. The EHR
**verifies** each DVC offline against that copy ([STT-VER-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-001)…[009](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-009),
[STT-KID-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-kid-002)), without contacting Thailand. Both verify, so it imports them as
FHIR `Immunization`s (`TrustDemoJ3HepB`, `TrustDemoJ3Bcg`) with provenance
(`TrustDemoJ3Verification`; [STT-VER-007](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-007), [STT-VER-008](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-008)), replacing the reported
doses of J2. If a DVC fails (a tampered card, say), the EHR names the step and
the reason, the doses stay unverified, and the nurse decides by national
catch-up policy.

**J3b.** The Thai Hep B product matches nothing on the national schedule.
The EHR keeps Thailand's product coding and adds the schedule coding beside
it, from the national map (`TrustDemoProductToLaoEpi`). For the Hep B product
the map has no entry, so Nurse Chanthasone makes the clinical call that it is
the schedule's birth dose (`TrustDemoJ3Adjudication`), and her decision is
added to the map for the next clinic. The schedule (`TrustDemoLaoInfantSchedule`)
then runs: the birth doses count, and pentavalent 1, bOPV 1 and PCV 1 are due
at 6 weeks (`TrustDemoJ3Recommendation`). Khamla leaves with the date
(`TrustDemoJ3Reminder`). Over the year Somsack gets those doses and
measles-rubella at 9 months, in Lao PDR.

- *Pain point:* clinicians either distrust foreign paper and re-vaccinate, or trust it blindly; and countries name and package vaccines differently.
- *Enabler:* Thailand's key is on the shared WHO trust list, so any clinic checks it locally; the original code is kept and the national code added beside it.
- *Policy:* trust is decentralized: a Lao clinic verifies a Thai signature itself. Never overwrite another country's record.

#### J4.0 — Crossing back: one family, one phone (Lao PDR, 12 months later)

**Precondition, as in J1:** Country B's DSC, under Country B's CSCA, is
already shared with the GDHCN, the Trust Anchor. That is what lets the
clinic in Thailand verify the link in J4.1.

**J4.0a.** The family plans a trip to Thailand. Bounmy's phone holds the
family wallet, with a profile for each of them. Somsack's summary
(`TrustDemoJ4Ips`) shows six doses: two from Thailand, four from Lao PDR.

**J4.0b.** For Somsack, Bounmy shares his record with a 4-digit passcode he
can say aloud, valid for 14 days. The portal records his consent
(`TrustDemoJ4Consent`), then does three things:

1. It assembles the IPS and Somsack's DVCs.
2. It encrypts them ([STT-VHL-004](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-004), [STT-VHL-007](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-007)) behind a passcode-protected manifest with an expiry ([STT-VHL-009](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-009)).
3. It issues the link as an HCERT, with the VHL at key 5 ([STT-VHL-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-001), [STT-VHL-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-002)), signed with Country B's DSC.

The QR holds only a pointer and a key: the record stays in Lao PDR.

- *Pain point:* many families share one smartphone, and photos or PDFs of records leak data and cannot be verified.
- *Enabler:* a household wallet on one phone with a summary per person; a Verifiable Health Link whose data stays home until the passcode is given.
- *Policy:* design for shared devices; data sovereignty: the record stays home until the family authorizes someone to open it.

#### J4.1 — Crossing back: a Thai doctor sees the full history (Chiang Rai, 12 months later)

**Precondition, as in J3: the DID documents are already loaded.** The
clinic viewer's trust store is a cached copy of the GDHCN trust list,
including Country B's DSC DID document ([STT-TRU-001](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-001), [STT-TRU-002](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-002),
[STT-TRU-005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-tru-005)). The clinic refreshes it nightly or hourly, against about
weekly at the offline J3 clinic. It does not need to be online to verify:
verifying reads the cache and never fetches the list. A DSC published after
the last refresh fails the trust-list check ([STT-VER-006](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-006)), naming that reason.

Back where it began, Dr Somchai sees Somsack at a primary care clinic in
Chiang Rai. Bounmy shows the QR on his phone and says the passcode. The
clinic viewer and the Lao gateway take five steps:

1. The viewer verifies the HCERT against Country B's DSC in its copy of the trust list.
2. It requests the manifest by ITI-YY5, signed with HTTP Message Signatures ([STT-VHL-005](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-005), [STT-VHL-006](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-006), [STT-VHL-008](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-008)).
3. The Lao gateway checks the passcode, the expiry and the consent, returns the manifest, and logs the access at home (`TrustDemoJ41Access`).
4. The viewer decrypts the IPS and DVCs ([STT-VHL-007](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-vhl-007)) (`TrustDemoJ41Received`).
5. It shows them to Dr Somchai: every dose since the birth, viewed, never copied.

A wrong passcode is refused, and the attempt is still logged in Lao PDR
(`TrustDemoJ41WrongPasscode`). If the HCERT does not verify (for example,
Country B's DSC is missing from the cached list), there is no digital
verification. The clinic names the step and the reason ([STT-VER-008](https://litlfred.github.io/smart-trust-tools/viewers/requirements.html#stt-ver-008)), does not
follow the VHL, and Dr Somchai treats whatever the family can show as he
would a paper record.

- *Pain point:* without the history, the doctor would repeat vaccines or have to guess.
- *Enabler:* the record is fetched live from Lao PDR, viewed without being copied, and an access log is kept at home.
- *Policy:* continuity of care across borders, with no central database, no international patient registry and no vendor lock-in.
